        <min>
            <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/fuel-kg-s</property>
            <product>
                <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/outflow-kg-s</property>
                <value>0.080000000000000002</value>
            </product>
        </min>
    </function>
    <function name="fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[#]/total-temperature-k" type="pre">
        <quotient>
            <sum>
                <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/outflow-enthalpy-w</property>
                <product>
                    <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/burned-fuel-kg-s</property>
                    <value>36000000</value>
                </product>
            </sum>
            <max>
                <value>9.9999999999999998e-13</value>
                <product>
                    <sum>
                        <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/outflow-kg-s</property>
                        <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/fuel-kg-s</property>
                    </sum>
                    <value>1150</value>
                </product>
            </max>
        </quotient>
    </function>
    <function name="fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[#]/pressure-ratio" type="pre">
        <max>
            <value>1</value>
            <product>
                <value>0.84999999999999998</value>
                <pow>
                    <quotient>
                        <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/outflow-enthalpy-w</property>
                        <max>
                            <value>9.9999999999999998e-13</value>
                            <product>
                                <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/outflow-kg-s</property>
                                <value>558.05555555555554</value>
                                <property>atmosphere/T-R</property>
                            </product>
                        </max>
                    </quotient>
                    <value>3.5</value>
                </pow>
            </product>
        </max>
    </function>
    <function name="fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[#]/exit-speed-m-s" type="pre">
        <sqrt>
            <max>
                <value>0</value>
                <product>
                    <value>2300</value>
                    <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/total-temperature-k</property>
                    <difference>
                        <value>1</value>
                        <pow>
                            <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/pressure-ratio</property>
                            <value>-0.24812030075187974</value>
                        </pow>
                    </difference>
                </product>
            </max>
        </sqrt>
    </function>
    <function name="fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[#]/gross-thrust-n" type="pre">

            </sum>
            <property>fsim/ducted-inlet-v2/engine[1]/exit-speed-m-s</property>
        </product>
    </function>

theory.limits: NASA ideal rocket equation omits drag/gravity/pressure trajectory coupling and is only a mass/impulse oracle. Ducted closure is a reduced inlet/combustor/nozzle model, not an OEM Meteor map or shock-resolved inlet. Commandable dual pulse differs physically from an uninterrupted single mass-axis burn. Native flow/starvation and finite state timing remain actual production authority.
theory.delta: PL15/R37M require actual hybrid commandable-pulse state/epoch comparison; Meteor requires matched finite-inlet mass/enthalpy/momentum and transient comparison. These are additional to ordinary solid impulse checks, not aliases of them.
theory.state: Solid native expended-propellant/burn-time, actual fuel and thrust tables. Dual pulse adds requested/expired/cache/monotonic-time state using admitted speed/time-to-go, finite hold and actual remaining fuel. Meteor adds matched mass/enthalpy/momentum residence filters and actual resident native mass plus actual consumed-fuel heat.
theory.io: Explicit per-card motor phases/Isp/build-up/coast settings and real native fuel -> thrust, flow, mass/CG/inertia; optional pulse decision -> native commanded phase only. Ducted inlet uses actual own air-relative velocity/density/temperature/Mach and actual fuel flow; no target truth.
theory.discretization: Native solid build-up uses sine ramp; table axis and engine-consumption conventions are source-bound. Pulse manager does not advance its own synthetic motor. Ducted V2 residence filters use trapezoidal integration, admitted native dt<=2*tau for positivity, matched inventory/flux ledgers; nozzle is reduced perfect-gas equivalent expansion.
theory.uncertainty: Three mechanism cohorts:21 ordinary solid,2 commandable dual-pulse,1 finite-inlet ducted. Each phase/Isp/geometry/pulse/inlet parameter keeps original source/basis/nonzero uncertainty; generic assumed Isp is not measured hardware calibration. Finite inventory tests do not admit the entire flight envelope.

theory.limits: NASA ideal rocket equation omits drag/gravity/pressure trajectory coupling and is only a mass/impulse oracle. Ducted closure is a reduced inlet/combustor/nozzle model, not an OEM Meteor map or shock-resolved inlet. Commandable dual pulse differs physically from an uninterrupted single mass-axis burn. Native flow/starvation and finite state timing remain actual production authority.
theory.delta: PL15/R37M require actual hybrid commandable-pulse state/epoch comparison; Meteor requires matched finite-inlet mass/enthalpy/momentum and transient comparison. These are additional to ordinary solid impulse checks, not aliases of them.
theory.state: Solid native expended-propellant/burn-time, actual fuel and thrust tables. Dual pulse adds requested/expired/cache/monotonic-time state using admitted speed/time-to-go, finite hold and actual remaining fuel. Meteor adds matched mass/enthalpy/momentum residence filters and actual resident native mass plus actual consumed-fuel heat.
theory.io: Explicit per-card motor phases/Isp/build-up/coast settings and real native fuel -> thrust, flow, mass/CG/inertia; optional pulse decision -> native commanded phase only. Ducted inlet uses actual own air-relative velocity/density/temperature/Mach and actual fuel flow; no target truth.
theory.discretization: Native solid build-up uses sine ramp; table axis and engine-consumption conventions are source-bound. Pulse manager does not advance its own synthetic motor. Ducted V2 residence filters use trapezoidal integration, admitted native dt<=2*tau for positivity, matched inventory/flux ledgers; nozzle is reduced perfect-gas equivalent expansion.
theory.uncertainty: Three mechanism cohorts:21 ordinary solid,2 commandable dual-pulse,1 finite-inlet ducted. Each phase/Isp/geometry/pulse/inlet parameter keeps original source/basis/nonzero uncertainty; generic assumed Isp is not measured hardware calibration. Finite inventory tests do not admit the entire flight envelope.
